I2.quote: After the carbonization step, the carbon microspheres (CS) are mainly composed by C, i.e. >90 wt%, with a very low O content.

I4.quote: For BO < 66 wt%, the materials exhibit BET surface areas below ~2500 m2 g− 1, while for larger BOs, ultra-high BET surface area in the range of 3000–3300 m2 g− 1 are achievable.

I5.quote: Highly porous carbon microspheres have been obtained by a sustainable and facile approach that combines a microwave-assisted sol-gel process with a physical activation process.

notes: Measured sorbents are CO2-activated carbon microspheres CS-x-y; Table S1 (si1, p. 1) gives C 93.92-94.38 wt% for activated samples, so carbon is the majority component. Uptakes are reported as total ('All isotherms and reported uptake data in this work are in terms of total adsorption', main p. 3, Section 2.3), converted from net/excess using He skeletal density and single-point pore volume. An additional gravimetric isotherm at -123 C up to 40 bar was measured for CS-885-82 (Fig. S9); -123 C 5 bar values in Table 3 are theoretical (Toth prediction).
